content:
Let the cylinder be \(x^2+y^2\le 100,\ 0\le z\le 3\), and the cube be \([-3,3]^2\times[-6,0]\).

For \(0\le z\le 3\), the convex hull’s cross-section is just the disk of radius \(10\), since the cube’s square cross-section lies inside it. So this part contributes
\[
3\cdot 100\pi=300\pi.
\]

For \(-6\le z\le 0\), set \(\alpha=-z/6\). The cross-section is
\[
\alpha S+(1-\alpha)B,
\]
where \(S\) is the square of side \(6\), and \(B\) is the disk of radius \(10\). By the Steiner formula,
\[
\operatorname{area}=36\alpha^2+24\alpha\cdot 10(1-\alpha)+100\pi(1-\alpha)^2.
\]
Thus the lower volume is
\[
6\int_0^1 \left(36\alpha^2+240\alpha(1-\alpha)+100\pi(1-\alpha)^2\right)\,d\alpha
=6\left(12+40+\frac{100\pi}{3}\right)
=312+200\pi.
\]
Total volume:
\[
V=312+200\pi+300\pi=312+500\pi.
\]
Therefore
\[
\lfloor V\rfloor=\lfloor 312+500\pi\rfloor=1882.
\]

\[
\boxed{1882}
\]
